newsitem.title: GERMANY: AMB says restructuring to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: AMB says restructuring to cut costs.

text.p: German insurer Aachener und Muenchener Beteiligungs-AG (AMB) said on Wednesday that it expected to save 400 million marks on annual costs as a result of its ongoing restructuring measures.
Chairman Wolfgang Kaske told a news conference that a whole series of cost-cuts were already secured for the current year, leading to savings of some 90 million marks.

AMB said earlier it expected satisfactory growth levels for 1997 and said it would at least match last year's group profits, provided there was not a drastic increase in claims and capital markets remained stable.
In 1996 AMB reported a group net profit of 343.3 million marks ($191.7 million).
However overall sales growth would probably slow to around four percent in the current year, Kaske warned, amid weak development in property and accident insurance.
AMB's 1996 premiums rose 5.4 percent to 17.1 billion marks.
Kaske said that in the current year, plans to centralise its computer systems would alone lead to savings of some 45 million marks.
It was only a matter of time before other costs savings kicked in, he added. The decisions had already been taken.
The company said its total premium income in the first five months of 1997 rose 5.4 percent to 7.8 billion marks.
Premium income in damage and accident insurance fell by 0.1 percent in the period, while life insurance new business grew above average by 3.5 percent. Health insurance also increased in the period.
AMB said it expected to pay an unchanged dividend in full-year 1997, despite an increase in base capital. In 1996 the dividend payout was increased to 16 marks per share from 15 marks per share.
AMB is planning to raise new capital as part of its restructuring process.
